question.text: Loss from exchange-traded derivatives can be set off against:

answer.text: Any income during the year except salary income

explanation.text: The Logic: Losses from exchange-traded derivatives are treated as normal (non-speculative) business loss and can be set off against income from any other head during the year EXCEPT salary income. The Trap: Salary is the only head against which this loss cannot be set off in the current year. The narrower wording "any business income except salary" is imprecise because salary is not business income in the first place. Note: Carry-forward treatment is separate — unabsorbed normal business loss carried forward can be set off only against business income in subsequent assessment years.
